sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin yajñe pravṛtte tu vāgmino hetuvādinaḥ hetuvādān bahūn prāhuḥ parasparajigīṣavaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When that sacrifice was under way, eloquent men skilled in reasoning, each eager to outdo the other, propounded many arguments of logic.

sanskrit: dadṛśus taṃ nṛpatayo yajñasya vidhim uttamam devendrasyeva vihitaṃ bhīmena kurunandana
english: The kings beheld that supreme rite of sacrifice, ordered by Bhīma as if it were the very rite of the lord of the gods, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: dadṛśus toraṇāny atra śātakumbhamayāni te śayyāsanavihārāṃś ca subahūn ratnabhūṣitān
english: There they saw archways wrought of gold, and very many couches, seats, and pleasure-halls adorned with jewels.

sanskrit: ghaṭān pātrīḥ kaṭāhāni kalaśān vardhamānakān na hi kiṃ cid asauvarṇam apaśyaṃs tatra pārthivāḥ
english: Pots, platters, cauldrons, water-jars, and covered vessels—the princes saw nothing there that was not made of gold.

sanskrit: yūpāṃś ca śāstrapaṭhitān dāravān hemabhūṣitān upakḷptān yathākālaṃ vidhivad bhūrivarcasaḥ
english: And the sacrificial posts, prescribed by scripture, made of wood and adorned with gold, were set up in due time and order, blazing with abundant splendor.

sanskrit: sthalajā jalajā ye ca paśavaḥ ke cana prabho sarvān eva samānītāṃs tān apaśyanta te nṛpāḥ
english: Whatever creatures there are, born of the land or born of the water, O lord—the kings saw them all brought together there.

sanskrit: gāś caiva mahiṣīś caiva tathā vṛddhāḥ striyo 'pi ca audakāni ca sattvāni śvāpadāni vayāṃsi ca
english: Cows and buffaloes, and aged women too, water-dwelling creatures, beasts of prey, and birds—

sanskrit: jarāyujāny aṇḍajāni svedajāny udbhidāni ca parvatānūpavanyāni bhūtāni dadṛśuś ca te
english: creatures born of the womb, born of the egg, born of sweat, and sprung from the soil, dwellers of mountains, marshlands, and forests—all these they beheld.

sanskrit: evaṃ pramuditaṃ sarvaṃ paśugodhanadhānyataḥ yajñavāṭaṃ nṛpā dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āgaman brāhmaṇānāṃ viśāṃ caiva bahumṛṣṭānnam ṛddhimat
english: Seeing the sacrificial enclosure thus everywhere rejoicing with cattle, herds, and grain, rich and abounding in plentiful well-dressed food for the brāhmaṇas and the common folk, the kings were filled with the highest wonder.

sanskrit: pūrṇe śatasahasre tu viprāṇāṃ tatra bhuñjatām dundubhir meghanirghoṣo muhur muhur atāḍyata
english: When a full hundred thousand brāhmaṇas were feasting there, the kettledrum, deep-voiced as a thundercloud, was struck again and again.

sanskrit: vinanādāsakṛt so 'tha divase divase tadā evaṃ sa vavṛte yajño dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ
english: Day after day it resounded without ceasing; thus did the sacrifice of the wise King of Righteousness proceed.

sanskrit: annasya bahavo rājann utsargāḥ parvatopamāḥ dadhikulyāś ca dadṛśuḥ sarpiṣaś ca hradāñjanāḥ
english: Many heaps of food, O king, like mountains were poured forth, and men saw streams of curds and lakes of clarified butter dark as collyrium.

sanskrit: jambūdvīpo hi sakalo nānājanapadāyutaḥ rājann adṛśyataikastho rājñas tasmin mahākratau
english: For the whole of Jambūdvīpa, thronged with its many peoples and realms, seemed gathered into one place, O king, at that great rite of the king.

sanskrit: tatra jātisahasrāṇi puruṣāṇāṃ tatas tataḥ gṛhītvā dhanam ājagmur bahūni bharatarṣabha
english: Thither came thousands upon thousands of men of every caste from this place and that, bringing much wealth, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: rājānaḥ sragviṇaś cāpi sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalāḥ paryaveṣan dvijāgryāṃs tāñ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And kings too, garlanded and wearing well-polished jeweled earrings, waited upon those foremost of the twice-born, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: vividhāny annapānāni puruṣā ye 'nuyāyinaḥ teṣāṃ nṛpopabhojyāni brāhmaṇebhyo daduḥ sma te
english: The various foods and drinks fit for a king's enjoyment, meant for the men who were their attendants, those kings gave away to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca samāgatān vedavido rājñaś ca pṛthivīśvarān dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bhīmasenam athābravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Seeing the knowers of the Veda assembled and the kings, the lords of the earth, King Yudhiṣṭhira then spoke to Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: upayātā naravyāghrā ya ime jagadīśvarāḥ eteṣāṃ kriyatāṃ pūjā pūjārhā hi nareśvarāḥ
english: "These tigers among men, these lords of the world, have come hither; let honor be done to them, for these rulers of men are worthy of honor."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tathā cakre narendreṇa yaśasvinā bhīmaseno mahātejā yamābhyāṃ saha bhārata
english: Thus addressed by the illustrious king, Bhīmasena of great splendor did accordingly, together with the twins, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: athābhyagacchad govindo vṛṣṇibhiḥ saha dharmajam baladevaṃ puraskṛtya sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Then Govinda, foremost of all living beings, approached the son of Dharma, accompanied by the Vṛṣṇis and with Baladeva at their head.

sanskrit: yuyudhānena sahitaḥ pradyumnena gadena ca niśaṭhenātha sāmbena tathaiva kṛtavarmaṇā
english: He came together with Yuyudhāna, with Pradyumna and Gada, with Niśaṭha and Sāmba, and likewise with Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: teṣām api parāṃ pūjāṃ cakre bhīmo mahābhujaḥ viviśus te ca veśmāni ratnavanti nararṣabhāḥ
english: To them too the mighty-armed Bhīma did the highest honor, and those bulls among men entered dwellings rich with jewels.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasamīpe tu kathānte madhusūdanaḥ arjunaṃ kathayām āsa bahusaṃgrāmakarśitam
english: And in Yudhiṣṭhira's presence, at the close of their converse, the Slayer of Madhu spoke of Arjuna, worn thin by his many battles.

sanskrit: sa taṃ papraccha kaunteyaḥ punaḥ punar ariṃdamam dharmarāḍ bhrātaraṃ jiṣṇuṃ samācaṣṭa jagatpatiḥ
english: The son of Kuntī, that subduer of foes, asked him again and again about his brother; and the Lord of the world, the King of Righteousness, told him of the victorious Jiṣṇu.

sanskrit: āgamad dvārakāvāsī mamāptaḥ puruṣo nṛpa yo 'drākṣīt pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaṃ bahusaṃgrāmakarśitam
english: "A trusted man of mine, a dweller in Dvārakā, came to me, O king, one who had seen the best of the Pāṇḍavas, worn thin by his many battles.

sanskrit: samīpe ca mahābāhum ācaṣṭa ca mama prabho kuru kāryāṇi kaunteya hayamedhārthasiddhaye
english: And he told me, O lord, that the mighty-armed one was near at hand: 'Carry out, O son of Kuntī, the preparations for the accomplishment of the horse-sacrifice.'"

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratyuvācainaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ diṣṭyā sa kuśalī jiṣṇur upayāti ca mādhava
english: Thus addressed, the King of Righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira, replied to him: "By good fortune the victorious one is well and is drawing near, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: tava yat saṃdideśāsau pāṇḍavānāṃ balāgraṇīḥ tad ākhyātum ihecchāmi bhavatā yadunandana
english: What that foremost in strength of the Pāṇḍavas sent word to you, that I wish to hear told here by you, O delight of the Yadus."

sanskrit: ity ukte rājaśārdūla vṛṣṇyandhakapatis tadā provācedaṃ vaco vāgmī dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: When this was said, O tiger among kings, the eloquent lord of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas then spoke these words to the righteous Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: idam āha mahārāja pārthavākyaṃ naraḥ sa mām vācyo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kṛṣṇa kāle vākyam idaṃ mama
english: "This message of Pārtha's, O great king, that man spoke to me: 'Yudhiṣṭhira is to be told, O Kṛṣṇa, in due time, this word of mine.

sanskrit: āgamiṣyanti rājānaḥ sarvataḥ kauravān prati teṣām ekaikaśaḥ pūjā kāryety etat kṣamaṃ hi naḥ
english: Kings will come from every quarter to the Kauravas; to each one of them honor should be done, for this is fitting for us.

sanskrit: ity etad vacanād rājā vijñāpyo mama mānada na tad ātyayikaṃ hi syād yad arghyānayane bhavet
english: By this word of mine the king is to be informed, O bestower of honor, lest there be any neglect in the offering of the guest-water.'"

sanskrit: kartum arhati tad rājā bhavāṃś cāpy anumanyatām rājadveṣād vinaśyeyur nemā rājan prajāḥ punaḥ
english: "The king ought to see to it, and let you also approve, lest through hostility to the kings these subjects of yours perish, O king."

sanskrit: idam anyac ca kaunteya vacaḥ sa puruṣo 'bravīt dhanaṃjayasya nṛpate tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: "And this other word of Dhanaṃjaya's that man spoke, O son of Kuntī; hear it, O king, as I declare it to you.

sanskrit: upayāsyati yajñaṃ no maṇipūrapatir nṛpaḥ putro mama mahātejā dayito babhruvāhanaḥ
english: 'To our sacrifice will come the king who is lord of Maṇipūra, my son of great splendor, my beloved Babhruvāhana.

sanskrit: taṃ bhavān madapekṣārthaṃ vidhivat pratipūjayet sa hi bhakto 'nuraktaś ca mama nityam iti prabho
english: Him you should duly honor for my sake, for he is ever devoted and attached to me'—so he said, O lord."

sanskrit: ity etad vacanaṃ śrutvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ abhinandyāsya tad vākyam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing these words, the King of Righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira, welcomed that speech of his and spoke these words.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrutaṃ priyam idaṃ kṛṣṇa yat tvam arhasi bhāṣitum tan me 'mṛtarasaprakhyaṃ mano hlādayate vibho
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have heard this pleasing word, O Kṛṣṇa, such as is worthy of you to speak; it is like the taste of nectar to me and gladdens my heart, O mighty lord.

sanskrit: bahūni kila yuddhāni vijayasya narādhipaiḥ punar āsan hṛṣīkeśa tatra tatreti me śrutam
english: Many battles, it is said, did Vijaya wage against kings, again and again here and there, so I have heard, O Hṛṣīkeśa.

sanskrit: mannimittaṃ hi sa sadā pārthaḥ sukhavivarjitaḥ atīva vijayo dhīmān iti me dūyate manaḥ
english: For my sake that wise Pārtha, Vijaya, has ever been deprived of comfort—at this exceedingly my mind grieves.

sanskrit: saṃcintayāmi vārṣṇeya sadā kuntīsutaṃ rahaḥ kiṃ nu tasya śarīre 'sti sarvalakṣaṇapūjite aniṣṭaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kṛṣṇa yena duḥkhāny upāśnute
english: I ever ponder in secret, O scion of Vṛṣṇi, upon the son of Kuntī: what unlucky mark can there be, O Kṛṣṇa, upon his body, honored with every auspicious sign, by reason of which he suffers such sorrows?

sanskrit: atīva duḥkhabhāgī sa satataṃ kuntinandanaḥ na ca paśyāmi bībhatsor nindyaṃ gātreṣu kiṃ cana śrotavyaṃ cen mayaitad vai tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Exceedingly does that son of Kuntī forever bear sorrow, yet I see nothing blameworthy in the limbs of Bībhatsu; if this is to be heard by me, you ought to explain it to me.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa hṛṣīkeśo dhyātvā sumahad antaram rājānaṃ bhojarājanyavardhano viṣṇur abravīt
english: Thus addressed, Hṛṣīkeśa, that Viṣṇu who is the increaser of the Bhoja royal line, having reflected a long while, spoke to the king.

sanskrit: na hy asya nṛpate kiṃ cid aniṣṭam upalakṣaye ṛte puruṣasiṃhasya piṇḍike 'syātikāyataḥ
english: "I perceive nothing inauspicious in this lion among men, O king, save that the calves of his legs are overly long.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ sa puruṣavyāghro nityam adhvasu yujyate na hy anyad anupaśyāmi yenāsau duḥkhabhāg jayaḥ
english: By reason of these that tiger among men is forever bound to journeys upon the roads; nothing else do I see by which Jaya bears such sorrow."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa kuruśreṣṭhas tathyaṃ kṛṣṇena dhīmatā provāca vṛṣṇiśārdūlam evam etad iti prabho
english: Thus told the truth by the wise Kṛṣṇa, that best of the Kurus replied to the tiger of the Vṛṣṇis: "It is even so," O lord.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇā tu draupadī kṛṣṇaṃ tiryak sāsūyam aikṣata pratijagrāha tasyās taṃ praṇayaṃ cāpi keśihā sakhyuḥ sakhā hṛṣīkeśaḥ sākṣād iva dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: But Kṛṣṇā, that is Draupadī, looked askance at Kṛṣṇa with some resentment, and the Slayer of Keśin accepted that fondness of hers; for Hṛṣīkeśa was a friend to his friend, even as another Dhanaṃjaya in the flesh.

sanskrit: tatra bhīmādayas te tu kuravo yādavās tathā remuḥ śrutvā vicitrārthā dhanaṃjayakathā vibho
english: There Bhīma and the rest, both Kurus and Yādavas, took delight in hearing the tales of Dhanaṃjaya, marvelous in their import, O lord.

sanskrit: tathā kathayatām eva teṣām arjunasaṃkathāḥ upāyād vacanān martyo vijayasya mahātmanaḥ
english: And even as they were thus telling stories of Arjuna, a mortal messenger came with word from the great-souled Vijaya.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya kuruśreṣṭhaṃ namaskṛtya ca buddhimān upāyātaṃ naravyāghram arjunaṃ pratyavedayat
english: Approaching the best of the Kurus and bowing to him, the prudent man announced that the tiger among men, Arjuna, was drawing near.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā nṛpatis tasya harṣabāṣpākulekṣaṇaḥ priyākhyānanimittaṃ vai dadau bahu dhanaṃ tadā
english: Hearing this, the king, his eyes brimming with tears of joy, then gave much wealth to him for the sake of that welcome tiding.

sanskrit: tato dvitīye divase mahāñ śabdo vyavardhata āyāti puruṣavyāghre pāṇḍavānāṃ dhuraṃdhare
english: Then on the second day a great clamor swelled up as that tiger among men, the foremost bearer of the Pāṇḍavas' burden, drew near.

sanskrit: tato reṇuḥ samudbhūto vibabhau tasya vājinaḥ abhito vartamānasya yathoccaiḥśravasas tathā
english: Then the dust that arose shone about his steed as it moved, even as it does about Uccaiḥśravas.

sanskrit: tatra harṣakalā vāco narāṇāṃ śuśruve 'rjunaḥ diṣṭyāsi pārtha kuśalī dhanyo rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: There Arjuna heard the joyful murmuring voices of the people: "By good fortune you are safe, O Pārtha; blessed is King Yudhiṣṭhira!

sanskrit: ko 'nyo hi pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnām avajitya sapārthivām cārayitvā hayaśreṣṭham upāyāyād ṛte 'rjunam
english: For who other than Arjuna, having conquered the whole earth with its kings and let the finest of horses roam free, could return again?"

sanskrit: ye vyatītā mahātmāno rājānaḥ sagarādayaḥ teṣām apīdṛśaṃ karma na kiṃ cid anuśuśruma
english: "Of the great-souled kings who have passed away, Sagara and the rest, not even of them have we heard of any such deed as this.

sanskrit: naitad anye kariṣyanti bhaviṣyāḥ pṛthivīkṣitaḥ yat tvaṃ kurukulaśreṣṭha duṣkaraṃ kṛtavān iha
english: Nor will the kings of the earth yet to come accomplish this hard deed that you, O best of the Kuru race, have done here."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vadatāṃ teṣāṃ nṝṇāṃ śrutisukhā giraḥ śṛṇvan viveśa dharmātmā phalguno yajñasaṃstaram
english: Hearing the words of the people thus speaking, sweet to his ears, the righteous Phalguna entered the sacrificial enclosure.

sanskrit: tato rājā sahāmātyaḥ kṛṣṇaś ca yadunandanaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ puraskṛtya te taṃ pratyudyayus tadā
english: Then the king with his counsellors, and Kṛṣṇa the delight of the Yadus, putting Dhṛtarāṣṭra at their head, went forth then to meet him.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya pituḥ pādau dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ bhīmādīṃś cāpi saṃpūjya paryaṣvajata keśavam
english: Saluting the feet of his father and of the wise King of Righteousness, and honoring Bhīma and the rest, he embraced Keśava.

sanskrit: taiḥ sametyārcitas tān sa pratyarcya ca yathāvidhi viśaśrāmātha dharmātmā tīraṃ labdhveva pāragaḥ
english: Honored by them as they met him, and honoring them in return as was due, the righteous one rested then, like a crosser of the waters who has gained the farther shore.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu sa rājā babhruvāhanaḥ mātṛbhyāṃ sahito dhīmān kurūn abhyājagāma ha
english: At this very time the wise King Babhruvāhana, together with his two mothers, came to the Kurus.

sanskrit: sa sametya kurūn sarvān sarvais tair abhinanditaḥ praviveśa pitāmahyāḥ kuntyā bhavanam uttamam
english: Having met all the Kurus and being welcomed by them all, he entered the excellent abode of his grandmother Kuntī.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa praviśya yathānyāyaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ niveśanam pitāmahīm abhyavadat sāmnā paramavalgunā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having duly entered the dwelling of the Pāṇḍavas, he greeted his grandmother with the most gracious courtesy.

sanskrit: tathā citrāṅgadā devī kauravyasyātmajāpi ca pṛthāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ ca sahite vinayenābhijagmatuḥ subhadrāṃ ca yathānyāyaṃ yāś cānyāḥ kuruyoṣitaḥ
english: And likewise Queen Citrāṅgadā, together with the daughter of the Kauravya, approached with humility Pṛthā and Kṛṣṇā, and Subhadrā in due form, and the other women of the Kurus.

sanskrit: dadau kuntī tatas tābhyāṃ ratnāni vividhāni ca draupadī ca subhadrā ca yāś cāpy anyā daduḥ striyaḥ
english: Then Kuntī gave to the two of them jewels of various kinds, and Draupadī and Subhadrā and the other women gave gifts as well.

sanskrit: ūṣatus tatra te devyau mahārhaśayanāsane supūjite svayaṃ kuntyā pārthasya priyakāmyayā
english: There the two queens dwelt upon costly beds and seats, well honored by Kuntī herself out of her wish to please Pārtha.

sanskrit: sa ca rājā mahāvīryaḥ pūjito babhruvāhanaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahīpālam upatasthe yathāvidhi
english: And that king of great valor, Babhruvāhana, being honored, waited duly upon Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the ruler of the earth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca rājānaṃ bhīmādīṃś cāpi pāṇḍavān upagamya mahātejā vinayenābhyavādayat
english: And approaching King Yudhiṣṭhira and Bhīma and the other Pāṇḍavas, the one of great splendor saluted them with humility.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ premṇā pariṣvaktaḥ pūjitaś ca yathāvidhi dhanaṃ cāsmai dadur bhūri prīyamāṇā mahārathāḥ
english: Embraced by them with affection and duly honored, he was given abundant wealth by those great chariot-warriors, well pleased with him.

sanskrit: tathaiva sa mahīpālaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ cakragadādharam pradyumna iva govindaṃ vinayenopatasthivān
english: And likewise that ruler of the earth waited with humility upon Kṛṣṇa, the bearer of discus and mace, even as Pradyumna waits upon Govinda.

sanskrit: tasmai kṛṣṇo dadau rājñe mahārham abhipūjitam rathaṃ hemapariṣkāraṃ divyāśvayujam uttamam
english: To that king Kṛṣṇa gave a costly and much-prized chariot, adorned with gold and yoked with celestial horses, the finest of its kind.

sanskrit: dharmarājaś ca bhīmaś ca yamajau phalgunas tathā pṛthak pṛthag atīvainaṃ mānārhaṃ samapūjayan
english: And the King of Righteousness and Bhīma, the twins and Phalguna, each in turn, honored him exceedingly, for he was worthy of honor.

sanskrit: tatas tṛtīye divase satyavatyāḥ suto muniḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ samabhyetya vāgmī vacanam abravīt
english: Then on the third day the sage, the son of Satyavatī, the eloquent one, came to Yudhiṣṭhira and spoke these words.

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti kaunteya yajasva samayo hi te muhūrto yajñiyaḥ prāptaś codayanti ca yājakāḥ
english: "From this day onward, O son of Kuntī, perform your sacrifice, for your time has come; the auspicious moment for the rite is at hand, and the officiating priests are urging it on.

sanskrit: ahīno nāma rājendra kratus te 'yaṃ vikalpavān bahutvāt kāñcanasyāsya khyāto bahusuvarṇakaḥ
english: This rite of yours, O lord of kings, named Ahīna and offering choices, is renowned as the Bahusuvarṇaka, the 'rich-in-gold,' because of the abundance of its gold.

sanskrit: evam eva mahārāja dakṣiṇāṃ triguṇāṃ kuru tritvaṃ vrajatu te rājan brāhmaṇā hy atra kāraṇam
english: Even so, O great king, make the priestly fee threefold; let it come to threefold, O king, for the brāhmaṇas are the cause herein.

sanskrit: trīn aśvamedhān atra tvaṃ saṃprāpya bahudakṣiṇān jñātivadhyākṛtaṃ pāpaṃ prahāsyasi narādhipa
english: By attaining herein three horse-sacrifices with abundant fees, you will cast off the sin incurred by the slaying of kinsmen, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: pavitraṃ paramaṃ hy etat pāvanānāṃ ca pāvanam yad aśvamedhāvabhṛthaṃ prāpsyase kurunandana
english: For this purifying bath at the close of the horse-sacrifice, which you shall attain, O delight of the Kurus, is the supreme purifier, the cleanser of cleansers."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tu tejasvī vyāsenāmitatejasā dīkṣāṃ viveśa dharmātmā vājimedhāptaye tadā narādhipaḥ prāyajata vājimedhaṃ mahākratum
english: Thus addressed by Vyāsa of measureless splendor, that splendid and righteous one then entered upon the consecration for the attaining of the horse-sacrifice; and the ruler of men offered up the horse-sacrifice, that great rite.
